texts.preamble: Abdul Razak Alias K M Razak Perla vs Faiz Ul Main on 7 November, 2025 1 O.S.No.7579/2023 Kabc010311162023 In The Court Of Xxxix Additional City Civil & Sessions Judge, (Cch-40), Bengaluru City. Present: Mamtaz, M.A., Ll.B., P.G.D.C.A. Xxxix Additional City Civil & Sessions Judge, Bengaluru City. Dated: This the 07th day of November 2025 O.S. No.7579/2023 Plaintiff : Mr. Abdul Razak @ K.M. Razak Perla, Aged about 56 Years, S/ o Sri. Abdulla Thawakkal, R/at No. 21, S.N. Plaza Complex, N.H. Main Road, Kalasipalya, Bengaluru - 560 002
texts.facts: This is a suit for permanent injunction and other consequential reliefs. 2. Brief facts of the plaintiffs case is that, the Plaintiff was the tenant under one Sri. Sadiq Patel i.e., the father of the Defendants herein in respect of the Shop bearing No. 35, Old No.572/ 6, situated at OTC Road, Cottonpet, Bengaluru, measuring 10 Feet x 13 Feet, totally measuring 130 Sq. Ft., along with rolling shutter, electricity facility and water facility, more vividly described in the Schedule hereunder written and hereinafter referred to as the Schedule Premises. That originally the Schedule Premises belonged to one Sri. Sadiq Patel i.e., the father of the Defendants herein and earlier the building existing thereon was old and the Plaintiff herein had obtained the Schedule premises on a monthly rent from the father of the Defendants Sri. Sadiq Patel by way of entering into Shop Rent Agreement dated: 05.09.2009 on a monthly rent of Rs. 6,000/- per month and he had paid a sum of Rs. 1,00,000/- as advance sale consideration. That ever since from the date of taking the Schedule Premises on Rent i.e., from September 2009, the Plaintiff herein was running a Tea Stall with Snacks under the name and style of Karnataka Tea Stall and at no point of time the Plaintiff had defaulted in payment of rent and he was regular in the same, such being the factual position, Sri. Sadiq Patel passed away, leaving behind the Plaintiffs as his heirs to succeed his estate, accordingly the tenancy stood attorned to the defendants and the Plaintiff continued to be tenant under the defendants and the Plaintiff was continuing as a tenant uninterruptedly. 3. It is further submitted that, when this being the factual position, recently while the adjacent building owner was renovating/ repairing his building premises, since the building existing on the Schedule Premises was old and was in dilapidated condition, the same fell down at that point of time the defendants herein expressed their inability to construct/ renovate the Schedule Premises for want of money and requested the Plaintiff to invest his own money and construct the building on the Schedule Premises and continue in the said premises as tenant therein by paying additional security deposit and increase in the rent. It is submitted that since the Plaintiff was doing business in the Schedule Premises for more than a decade and the employees therein were entirely depending on the earnings derived in the Schedule Premises for their livelihood, having no other alternative the Plaintiff at his cost and expenses had got renovated/ reconstructed the building on the Schedule Premises and thereafter continued business in the Schedule Premises under the name and style of Karnataka Tea Centre. It is further submitted that, subsequent to renovating the building on the Schedule Premises, when the Plaintiff approached the defendants so as to execute Rental Agreement afresh, at that point of time the defendants demanded the Plaintiff to pay additional sum of Rs.4,00,000/- as security deposit and to pay a sum of Rs. 12,000/- as monthly rent, on the demand so made, the Plaintiff having no other alternative agreed for the same with an intention to maintain cordial relationship and upon receipt of the payment, the Defendants executed a fresh Rental Agreement on 27.07.2022 acknowledging to have received a sum of Rs. 5,00,000/- as security deposit which sum includes security deposit of Rs. 1,00,000/ - paid under the Rent Agreement dtd: 05.09.2000 and the Rental Agreement was for a period of Eleven (11) months commencing from 01.08.2022 and it was specifically agreed that the said agreement shall be mutually extended for further period with increased rent by 10% on completion of every eleven months. That on cursory perusal of the above said facts, it is clear that the Plaintiff is tenant in respect of the Schedule Premises since from the year 2009 and at his own cost and expenses has got the Schedule Property renovated/ reconstructed and that apart has also paid a huge sum of Rs. 5,00,000/- as security deposit, such being the factual position, on 02.11.2023 the defendants herein for the reasons best known by colluding with their men, agents, henchmen with an intention to harass and humiliate the Plaintiff for no fault of him with a sole object of dispossessing the Plaintiff and his employees from the Schedule Premises so as to gain illegally and also to cause wrongful loss to the Plaintiff herein, notwithstanding the fact of the Plaintiff having got the building constructed thereon, but the said act of the defendants, their agents and their henchmen was successfully restrained by the Plaintiff. The plaintiff filed false suit against the defendants herein.
texts.arguments: 5. It is further submitted that, the defendants along with their henchmen, agents and third persons are threatening the plaintiff to dispossess him and his employees from the Schedule Premises by using money and muscle power. The defendants and their henchmen have scant respect for law and they wield anti-social and political clout and may stoop to any level to see that their illegal designs are put into action. The defendants in furtherance of their illegal designs had threatened the Plaintiff on 18.11.2023 that unless the Plaintiff vacate the schedule Premises by the end of this month, they would physically throw him out of the Schedule Premises at that point of time the Plaintiff expressed his intention to continue as a tenant therein and also brought to the notice about the fact of the Plaintiff having renovated the building at his own cost and expenses, for which the defendants started acting otherwise and expressed their ill intention to continue the Plaintiff as his tenant and also contrary to the terms of the Agreement. It is relevant here to state that as per the Agreement, it is clear that the provision for earlier termination is only by way of issuing at least 3 months advance intimating his intention, then only the Defendants are entitled to terminate the agreement and take repossession of the Premises and that there is a specific clause of renewing the Agreement for a further period, but in the present case on hand at no point of time the Plaintiff has committed default. 6. It is further submitted that, he is a tenant under the Defendants and the Rental Agreement dated: 01.08.2022 so entered between the parties has not been terminated and the defendants have been accepting the rents without any protest, further at no point of time the Defendant has issued any prior notice as envisaged under law, such being the factual position, the Plaintiff has all rights to continue in the Schedule premises without any hindrance from the defendants or their henchmen, agents, etc., That, notwithstanding the facts as aforesaid it is evident that on 18.11.2023 the Abdul Razak Alias K M Razak Perla vs Faiz Ul Main on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190677447/ 3 defendants herein through their agents without having any manner of right and contrary to the law of land had approached the Plaintiff and demanded him to vacate the Schedule Premises forthwith, failing which they would break open the lock and put another lock and also tried to dispossess/ trespass and threaten the Plaintiff of dire consequences without following due process of law, but the said act of defendant and his henchmen was successfully restrained by the Plaintiff and his family members. It is submitted that, the Plaintiff is a Tenant and is entitled to continue in the Schedule Premises as a Tenant therein, notwithstanding the same, the defendants without any reason along with their agents and henchmen are trying to interfere with the possession of the Plaintiff over the Schedule premises without following due process of law, such being the facts, the act of the defendants is not at all sustainable in the eye of law and that apart the Plaintiff being unable to continuously restrain the illegal act of the defendants are approaching this Hon'ble Court for redressal of their grievances. Hence this suit. 7. After receipt of the suit summons, the defendants appeared through their counsel and filed written statement and denied the plaint averments and submitted that, the suit is not maintainable either in law or on facts. The cause of action is false and baseless. The plaintiff has filed this suit deliberately and intentionally in order to harass these defendants. The plaintiff has suppressed and misrepresented the facts in the above suit and he has not come before the court with clean hands. The Plaintiff was a tenant under the true father of the Defendants namely Sri. Sadiq Patel, in respect of the Suit Schedule Shop. Originally the Suit Schedule Shop premises belong to the father of these Defendants namely Sri. Sadiq Patel on monthly rent of Rs.6,000/- with the security deposit amount of Rs.1,00,000/-. The Plaintiff has played fraud by sub- letting the Suit Schedule Shop premises to one Sri. Saheed without the knowledge of Sri. Sadiq Patel and without the knowledge of the Defendants herein. Sri. Sadiq Patel passed away on 26-6-2017 leaving behind the Defendants herein as his only legal heirs to succeed to the Suit Schedule Shop premises. The Defendants herein are young boys and they are now aged about 25 years and 22 years respectively. These Defendants who are young boys are not conversant with the law and procedures. Taking undue advantage of tender age of the Defendants, lack of legal knowledge of these Defendants, the Plaintiff has played fraud by taking their signature in the rental agreement dated: 01-8- 2022 and without explaining the contents of the said rental agreement which is produced by the Plaintiff himself. The Defendants have not received the alleged Security Deposit of Rs.5,00,000/- under the said agreement. Hence, the Plaintiff has suppressed the true facts. 8. It is further submitted that, initially at the inception of tenancy the Plaintiff was doing the business in the Suit Schedule Shop premises. But he has clandestinely sub - let the Suit Schedule Shop premises to Sri. Saheed and the said Sri. Saheed was paying the rents to these Defendants father, as also paying the rents to these Defendants. The Registration Certificate issued by the Govt. of Karnataka, Department of Food Safety and Standards Authority to run the tea stall has been issued in the name of a third person namely Sri. Zakaria. P on the Suit Schedule address. Hence, the Plaintiff as well as the said Sri. Saheed have inducted Sri. Zakaria P. in the possession of the Suit Schedule Shop premises. The screenshots of the online payment of the monthly rents to the Defendant No.1 dated 08-01-2023, 07.07.2023 and 09-10-2023 by S. Abdul Saheed has been produced by the Plaintiff himself with the Plaint , clearly established that Plaintiff is not paying the Abdul Razak Alias K M Razak Perla vs Faiz Ul Main on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190677447/ 4 monthly rents and the Plaintiff is not in actual possession of the Suit Schedule Shop premises either on the date of filing of the suit or prior to the date of filing of the suit. 9. It is further submitted that, plaintiff has not renovated/constructed the Suit Schedule Shop premises on his money. It is false to allege that the Defendants demanded additional security deposit of Rs.4,00,000/- from the Plaintiff. The monthly rent of Rs.12,000/- was voluntarily agreed by the Plaintiff himself. Hence, the Plaintiff has taken undue advantage of the innocence of these Defendants who are young boys and taking undue advantage of them has obtained their signature in the rental agreements. Hence, these Defendants specifically deny about the alleged payment of Rs.5,00,000/- as security deposit of the Suit Schedule Shop premises. The Plaintiff has not even given a copy of the rental agreements mentioned in the Paragraph No.8 of the Plaint to these Defendants. The Defendants are astonished to know about the contents of the rental agreement dated: 01-08-2022 produced by the Plaintiff in the above case. Hence, the Defendants have now come to know on receipt of the Plaint documents about the fraud and cheating done with them by the Plaintiff. 17. The plaintiff counsel vehemently argued that plaintiff was the tenant under Mr.Sadiq Patel who the father of the defendants and taken plaint schedule property on rent and is in possession of the same. The shop rent agreement was executed on 05.09.2009 for monthly rent of Rs.6,000/- and Rs.1,00,000/- refundable security deposit. 18. The defendants counsel vehemently argued that plaintiff is not in actual possession of the plaint schedule property but sub-let the premises to Sri.Saheed without the knowledge of Mr.Sadiq Patel and defendants. 21. The defendants counsel further submitted that after the death of Mr.Sadiq Patel the plaintiff took the signature of defendants upon rental agreement dated 01.08.2022 and they have not received Rs.5 lakhs security deposit.
